bio.en: Born to a farming family near Viljandi, he studied medicine in Kiev and served as a military physician in the First World War and the Estonian War of Independence. He became a well-known poet and radical socialist under the pen name Johannes Barbarus. After the Soviet occupation of June 1940, Andrei Zhdanov forced President Konstantin Päts to appoint him prime minister of a communist-dominated puppet government, and he headed the delegation that delivered the petition to join the Soviet Union. He then chaired the Estonian SSR Supreme Soviet’s presidium, fled to Soviet Russia when the Germans came in 1941, and after returning in 1944 was investigated by the NKVD over his role in the War of Independence. He died in the presidential residence in Kadriorg, Tallinn, in November 1946, most probably by suicide, though murder has also been suggested.

bio.en: Born the son of a tenant on a manor in Mazsalaca, Livonia, he studied at the Tartu Veterinary Institute, took part in the revolution of 1905 and emigrated to Switzerland, working at a tuberculosis institute in Davos. He served as a military veterinarian in the Serbian army in the First World War and as a captain in the veterinary units of the Latvian War of Independence. In 1919 he founded a Microbiology Institute at the University of Latvia, and in 1923 he defended the first doctoral thesis in Latvia; politically he supported social democracy. In June 1940 the Soviet embassy offered him the leadership of the new puppet government; as prime minister, and from 21 July acting president, he requested Latvia’s incorporation into the Soviet Union. He chaired the Latvian SSR Supreme Soviet’s presidium in 1940–1952, joined the Communist Party in 1941 and died in Riga in 1963.

bio.en: Born to a smallholding peasant family near Skapiškis, he studied law and was minister of defence (1919, 1926–1927), governor of the Klaipėda Region and mayor of Kaunas. After serving in autumn 1939 as government commissioner for the Vilnius region, he became prime minister that November, and in June 1940 he argued for accepting the Soviet ultimatum. When Smetona left the country he became acting president, announced on the radio the next day that he was now president in his own right, and on 17 June appointed Justas Paleckis prime minister and resigned. Lithuania regards this takeover of the presidency as unconstitutional. A month later he tried to escape to Sweden but was arrested in Riga and deported to Saratov; he was imprisoned in 1941. Released in 1954 but not allowed to return to Lithuania, he died in Vladimir in 1955.

bio.en: Born to a peasant family in the village of Subartonys in the Dzūkija region, he took his pen name from Krėvė, the name villagers gave his family. He received a doctorate in philology at Lviv in 1908, taught in Baku and in 1919 became Lithuania’s consul in Azerbaijan. From 1922 he taught Slavic literature at the University of Lithuania, and he is counted a classic of Lithuanian literature. After the Soviet occupation of June 1940 he joined the “People’s Government” as foreign minister and acting prime minister, but on the night of 1 July Molotov told him in Moscow that all the Baltic states had to join the Soviet Union; he returned and resigned. In 1941 he became the first president of the Lithuanian SSR Academy of Sciences. In July 1944 he left for Austria before the Soviets returned, and from 1947 he taught at the University of Pennsylvania until his death in 1954.

bio.en: Born in Riga to an Estonian trader and a Baltic German mother, he served in the Estonian Army during the Latvian War of Independence. He joined the Latvian foreign ministry in 1920, became its general secretary in 1933, ran the ministry de facto after Kārlis Ulmanis’s coup of 1934 and was foreign minister from 1936 to 1940; he was also active on the Council of the League of Nations. In June 1939 he signed the German–Latvian Non-Aggression Pact and on 5 October 1939 the Soviet–Latvian Mutual Assistance Treaty. After the Soviet occupation he and his family were deported to Voronezh in July 1940 in the presence of the interior minister Vilis Lācis; he was arrested in June 1941 and in 1952 sentenced to 25 years. Released in 1954, he returned to Latvia in 1958, wrote against the Latvian diaspora organisations and died in Riga in 1967.

bio.en: Born in New York City to a wealthy political family, he graduated from Harvard in 1914 and joined the diplomatic service on the advice of the family friend Franklin Roosevelt. A Latin America specialist, he saw his career ended by President Coolidge, but under Roosevelt he became Assistant Secretary for Latin American Affairs and then Under Secretary of State from 1937 to 1943. As acting Secretary of State he issued the Welles Declaration on 23 July 1940, condemning the Soviet occupation of the Baltic states and refusing to recognise their annexation; the day before, he had authorised diplomatic visas for the family of Konstantin Päts. He went on to oppose any concession on the Baltic question. He helped write the Atlantic Charter, but was forced out by Cordell Hull in 1943 after word spread that he had propositioned two railroad porters. He died in New Jersey in 1961.

bio.en: Born in 1893 in Reval (Tallinn), in the Governorate of Estonia of the Russian Empire, he studied architecture at the Riga Polytechnical Institute. In 1918 he left for Germany with the retreating German army and in January 1919 joined the German Workers’ Party, eight months before Hitler; in 1923 he became editor of the party newspaper Völkischer Beobachter. In 1930 he published his racial treatise The Myth of the Twentieth Century, and he fed Hitler’s belief in Jewish conspiracies by introducing him to The Protocols of the Elders of Zion. Appointed Reich Minister for the Occupied Eastern Territories on 17 July 1941, he had Hinrich Lohse installed as Reichskommissar for Ostland, though his own authority was severely limited. He saw the Baltic lands as German “Lebensraum”. Found guilty on all four counts at Nuremberg, he was hanged on 16 October 1946.

bio.en: Born into a peasant family in Schleswig-Holstein, he was severely wounded in the First World War. He joined the Nazi Party in 1923, became Gauleiter of Schleswig-Holstein in 1925 and in 1933 also Oberpräsident of the province. Appointed Reichskommissar for Ostland on 25 July 1941, he shuttled between Riga and Kiel; his decree of 27 July ordered lists of Jews, the yellow badge, the confiscation of their property and their concentration in ghettos. Asked to explain his order forbidding the execution of Jews in Libau (Liepāja), he wrote on 15 November asking whether all Jews were to be liquidated regardless of economic interests, yet he stayed at his post for three more years. He fled Ostland without authorisation on 13 August 1944 and was removed. Sentenced in 1948 to ten years, he was released for ill health in 1951 and died in his home village in 1964.

bio.en: Born into a pastor’s family in Sternenfels, he took a doctorate in law at Tübingen. He joined the Nazi Party and the SS in 1932, headed the Gestapo in Württemberg and then Breslau, and in 1938 became formal head of the Central Agency for Jewish Emigration in Vienna. Given command of Einsatzgruppe A in February 1941, he followed Army Group North into the Baltic states in June. He had Klimaitis start a pogrom in Kaunas and Arājs raise a unit in Riga, staging the killings as the “self-cleansing” of the local population. By the winter of 1941 he reported that Einsatzgruppe A had murdered some 249,420 Jews, and at the end of November he became commander of the Security Police and SD for Ostland. He was fatally wounded by Soviet partisans near Krasnogvardeysk, Russia, in March 1942.

From July 1941 to September 1943 he commanded Einsatzkommando 3 of Einsatzgruppe A in Kaunas, which with Lithuanian help shot Jewish men, women and children indiscriminately and carried out the Ninth Fort massacres of November 1941. When the Germans entered Riga in July 1941 he was introduced to Stahlecker and recruited a unit from his student fraternity and the Pērkonkrusts, which took part in burning Riga’s synagogues on 4 July. The Arajs Kommando murdered some 26,000 people in Latvia and then Belarus, and he was made an SS-Sturmbannführer in 1943. Interned in a British camp until 1949, he lived under a false name and worked at a printing company in Frankfurt. In 1979 the Hamburg State Court sentenced him to life imprisonment for leading the Jews of the Riga ghetto to their deaths on 8 December 1941; he died in prison in Kassel in 1988.

After standing twice for parliament he joined the Vaps movement as its propaganda chief; sentenced in 1935 to twenty years’ hard labour, he was amnestied in 1938, went to Germany and took German citizenship. In May 1941 he founded the Estonian Liberation Committee in Helsinki, and returning with the German army that year he headed the Estonian Self-Administration from 1941 to 1944. In 1944 he fled to Austria, where the Western Allies cleared him of Nazi crimes and he later advised the Austrian government. In the 1990s Estonia’s International Commission named him among the Estonians chiefly responsible for crimes committed by Estonian police and SS units.

bio.en: Born in Jelgava, he served in the Latvian Army’s artillery during the War of Independence in 1919–1920 and then worked as a docker in the port of Riga. Having witnessed the persecution of Jews in the streets, he resolved to save them, became a contractor for the Luftwaffe and from late November 1941 smuggled Jewish workers out of the Riga ghetto and nearby camps. With his wife Johanna and friends he hid them in warehouses and a bunker dug in his yard until the Red Army arrived in October 1944. The number saved is given as forty to about 55. After the war the KGB questioned him repeatedly. In 1966 Yad Vashem recognised him and his wife as Righteous Among the Nations, and when he died in 1987 the Jews of Riga arranged his funeral.

bio.en: Mobilised into the Imperial Russian Army in the First World War, he was the first to enlist in the Lithuanian armed forces after independence in 1918, and on 1 January 1919 his men raised the Lithuanian flag over Gediminas’ Tower in Vilnius. He became Chief of the General Staff in 1925 but had to resign after opposing the 1926 coup. He was envoy to Germany in 1927–1930 and 1938–1941. After the Soviet occupation of 1940 he founded in Berlin the Lithuanian Activist Front, which sought to restore independence by working with the Nazis; named prime minister of the provisional government in 1941, he was held under house arrest by the Germans. In 1944 he was arrested for a memorandum demanding a Lithuanian government. After the war he settled in the United States, working at the Library of Congress. His antisemitic writings have made dedications in his honour controversial.

bio.en: Born in Kirbla Parish in the Governorate of Estonia, he studied law at St Petersburg University and taught Roman and Estonian law at the University of Tartu until 1944. Editor-in-chief of Postimees and speaker of the lower chamber, he was prime minister from 1939 until Soviet troops entered Estonia in June 1940; after President Konstantin Päts was arrested by the Soviets he became, under the constitution, prime minister in the duties of the president. On 29 July 1941 he asked the Germans to let him form an independent government and was refused, and he declined to head the Self-Administration. On 7 February 1944 he appealed by radio for men to answer the call-up, and 38,000 registered. In June he appointed Otto Tief deputy prime minister, and in September, as the Germans withdrew, formed the Tief government. He then reached Sweden, where he died of gastric cancer in January 1945.

Arrested in the Great Purge in 1938, he was soon released without charges. During the German occupation he was the de facto leader of the Communist Party of Estonia and head of the Estonian partisan movement staff, and on 28 September 1944 he was elected First Secretary. He headed the central staff of the destruction battalions, and in March 1949 he briefed the county plenipotentiaries before the deportation. Removed after the Eighth Plenum of 1950 and replaced by Johannes Käbin, he worked in Moscow as an economist, took his doctorate in 1964, and, because of his disagreements with Käbin, never returned to Estonia; he died in Moscow in 1969.

bio.ko: 팔랑가에서 태어나 1929년 카우나스 군사학교를 마친 포병 장교로, 1936~1938년 프랑스 퐁텐블로의 포병학교에서 공부했다. 1941년 6월 누이의 가족이 시베리아로 추방되었고, 독일 점령기에는 나치에 복무하지 않으려 전역했다. 1944년 리투아니아 지역방위군에 들어갔고, 붉은군대가 돌아오자 리투아니아 자유군과 파르티잔에 합류해 지휘관으로 올라섰다. 1949년 2월 리투아니아 자유 전사 연합을 세워 의장이 되었고 부대를 통합하고 투쟁의 법적 틀을 마련했다. 1951년 12월 뇌출혈로 마비되었고 1953년 5월 30일 체포되어 모스크바에서 베리야의 심문을 받은 뒤 1954년 부티르카 감옥에서 처형되었다. 2009년 리투아니아 제4대 대통령으로 공식 인정되었다.
bio.en: Born in Palanga, he graduated from the War School of Kaunas in 1929 as an artillery officer and studied at the School of Applied Artillery in Fontainebleau, France, in 1936–1938. In the deportations of June 1941 his sister’s whole family was sent to Siberia; under the German occupation he retired rather than serve the Nazis. In 1944 he joined the Lithuanian Territorial Defense Force, and when the Red Army returned he joined the Lithuanian Liberty Army and the partisans, rising to the leadership. In February 1949 he founded the Union of Lithuanian Freedom Fighters and became its chairman, working to unify the partisan units and give their struggle a legal framework. Paralysed by a cerebral haemorrhage in December 1951, he was arrested on 30 May 1953, interrogated in Moscow by Beria and executed in Butyrka prison in 1954. In 2009 he was officially named the fourth President of Lithuania.

bio.ko: 미국 뉴브리튼의 리투아니아 이민 가정에서 태어나 세 살 때 리투아니아로 왔다. 1940년 카우나스 군사학교를 마치고 교사로 일하다, NKVD가 학생들을 감시하라고 압박하자 1945년 초 「바나가스」(매)라는 가명으로 파르티잔에 들어갔다. 다이나바 군관구와 남부 지역의 사령관을 지내며 지하 신문을 펴냈고, 1949년 리투아니아 자유 전사 연합 의장의 제1대리가 되었다. 1952년 요나스 제마이티스를 이어 연합을 이끌며 무장 투쟁을 멈추고 수동적 저항으로 돌아서라고 명령했다. 1956년 10월 옛 동창의 배신으로 체포되어 고문당한 뒤 1957년 11월 처형되었다. 1941년 6월 봉기 때 그가 지휘한 부대가 유대인 학살에 관여했다는 주장이 있으나 리투아니아 정부는 부인한다.
bio.en: Born to a Lithuanian immigrant family in New Britain, Connecticut, he came to Lithuania at the age of three. He graduated from the War School of Kaunas in 1940 and worked as a teacher, and after the NKVD pressured him to spy on his students he joined the partisans in early 1945 under the nom de guerre Vanagas (“Hawk”). He commanded the Dainava military district and the Southern Lithuania Region, published underground newspapers, and in 1949 became first deputy chairman of the Union of Lithuanian Freedom Fighters. Succeeding Jonas Žemaitis as its leader in 1952, he ordered an end to armed struggle in favour of passive resistance. Betrayed by a former classmate, he was arrested in October 1956, tortured and executed in November 1957. The Simon Wiesenthal Center has alleged that a unit he commanded in the June 1941 uprising took part in killing Jews; the Lithuanian government denies this.

bio.ko: 카우나스 근처 유오드부디스 마을의 농가에서 태어났다. 가톨릭 청년 단체 아테이티스와 극우·반유대·반소 단체 리투아니아 행동주의 전선(LAF)에 들어갔고, 1940~1941년 소련 점령기에 NKVD에 투옥되었다. 1944년부터 카우나스에서 지하 활동을 하다 1946년 무장 저항에 들어가 타우라스 군관구의 비루테 여단을 이끌었다. 1947년 말 철의 장막을 넘어 서방에 파르티잔의 자료를 전했고, 프랑스 정보기관과 CIA의 훈련을 받으며 『자유를 위한 투사들』을 썼다. 1949~1950년 낙하산으로 돌아왔다가 1951년 가을 파바르투피스 근처에서 MGB에 살해되었다. 목격자들은 그가 1941년 카우나스 리에투키스 차고 학살에 가담했다고 증언했으나 리투아니아 정부는 부인한다.
bio.en: Born to a farming family in the village of Juodbūdis near Kaunas, he joined the Catholic youth organisation Ateitis and the far-right, antisemitic and anti-Soviet Lithuanian Activist Front (LAF) at secondary school, and was imprisoned by the NKVD during the Soviet occupation of 1940–1941. After the Red Army returned in 1944 he worked in the Kaunas underground, joined the armed resistance in 1946 and commanded the Birutė brigade of the Tauras military district. At the end of 1947 he crossed the Iron Curtain with partisan documentation for the West, was trained by French intelligence and the CIA, and wrote Fighters for Freedom. Parachuted back by the CIA in 1949–1950, he was killed by the MGB near Pabartupis in the autumn of 1951. According to several witnesses he took part in the Lietūkis garage massacre in Kaunas in 1941; the Lithuanian government denies this.

bio.ko: 부유한 리투아니아 농가에서 태어나 상트페테르부르크, 세이니 신학교, 스위스 프리부르 대학에서 공부했다. 제1차 세계대전 때 러시아 제국군 군종 사제였고, 1927년부터 1940년 소련 점령으로 문을 닫을 때까지 텔샤이 신학교 교장을 지냈다. 1943년 텔샤이 교구장이 되었고, 1944년 서방으로 피하지 않았다. 파르티잔 지원 등의 혐의로 1945년 12월과 1946년 2월 NKVD에 체포되었으며, 협력하면 사면하겠다는 제안을 거절했다. 1946년 8월 28일 반역죄로 사형을 선고받아 11월 18일 처형된 것으로 여겨지며, 투스쿨레나이 영지의 집단 매장지에 묻혔다. 재판에서 유대인 세 사람이 그가 유대인을 숨겨 주었다고 증언했다. 1990년 시복 절차가 시작되었다.
bio.en: Born to a family of well-off Lithuanian farmers, he studied in Saint Petersburg, at the Sejny Priest Seminary and at the University of Fribourg in Switzerland. In the First World War he was a chaplain in the Russian Imperial Army, and from 1927 he was rector of the Telšiai priest seminary until the Soviet occupation closed it in 1940. He became bishop of Telšiai in 1943 and refused to retreat to the West in 1944. Accused of anti-Soviet activities including support for the partisans, he was arrested by the NKVD in December 1945 and again in February 1946, and refused an offer of a pardon in exchange for cooperation. Sentenced to death for treason on 28 August 1946, he is believed to have been executed on 18 November and was buried in a mass grave at Tuskulėnai Manor in Vilnius. At his trial three Jews testified that he had helped Jews hide. His beatification process began in 1990.
